title: How To Organize Your Clo Projects And Collaborate In Clo-Set
description: Level up your design processes with this quick overview of functions in CLO-SET. We have selected the best possibilities to help freelancers, students and hobbyists optimize their professional workflow.
transcript: Hello! In this video, we would like to share a quick overview of features in our platform Closet that are especially useful for freelancers and hobbyists using Clo. Closet is something like a Clo Cloud. It functions like a Dropbox or Drive for all your Clo projects, whether they are project files themselves or 3D garments, but also digitized fabrics, 3D trims, avatars, and so on. You can manage your 3D assets anytime from anywhere and collaborate with others, sharing feedback in real time. You can use it as a library for communication, garment presentation, and to organize collections. From your workspace, you can see all the content within your virtual closet as well as visual boards. Within rendering, you can see information of renders performed in the cloud. You will get back to both topics in a bit. There is a default closet structure for you to store your files, but it's not necessary. Closet can be reorganized and renamed. Within the general framework called Roop, you can create companies and within those companies, brands and workrooms. This way, you can organize your collections and clients in separate spaces. I have created a structure here containing a demo brand within a demo company, and the collection we are looking at right now is organized in a workroom called Denim. If you upload a project to Closet, a style page is created on which you have the following options. On the left, you will find style info such as date, creator, status, and notification options. You can upload and download versions of the project or garment file, generate tagpacks, and access the render settings of the file. Through the file history, you can track the evolution of a style as well as having the option to go back to a previous version if necessary, for example by uploading your updates to a file by the end of every day. In the middle, you see the 3D viewport with a turntable preview where you can annotate and switch between colorways. You can create annotations by clicking on the top right button, comment or draw and then press complete. Within the right column, you will find a list of all comments and annotations left on the style, as well as colorways, attachments, and to whom the style has been shared. Everything you add on Closet is protected and only viewable by those to whom you have granted access. As the administrator and creator of the structure, you can edit and delete anything within it. You can invite others as either editors or viewers. Editors can upload and download the files they have added. Viewers can only view but not edit. In addition to storage, the platform also provides a rendering function via the Closet server, so you don't have to do it on your own computer. This is especially useful if your own hardware does not have high specs or if you want to render without occupying your CLO license. So you can work on something else meanwhile. Any renders that you have created via the Closet servers will be accessible on the style page. You can use them to create your own style. As you can see on this project files viewport. Outside of our workroom and style pages, you can access the visual board section from your dashboard. Here you can create virtual mood boards and showcase your designs using 3D assets directly pulled from Closet. This removes the need for other visual workspaces and portfolio creation tools. And the final slides can contain interactive links connected to your assets. You can use them to create your own style. Simply drag and drop in your components from the content browser on the right. Change the colors of the background and add additional shapes. Add text and so on. As you categorize and work on your collections, you can filter through your workrooms and entire library quickly. For example, get an overview of all styles you have marked to adopt into the final lineup of your collection. Or filter by category such as specific product groups. You can also search through the tags you have given your styles. You can also search through the tags you have given your styles. If you are looking for more info on Closet and the many more functions within it that we have not covered here, please check out our in-depth tutorials and skill apps which can be found on the Chlo YouTube channel. As always, thank you for tuning in. Bye! Subtitles by the Amara.org community
markdown_content: ## Overview of Closet Platform for Clo Projects and Collaboration This section introduces Closet, a cloud-based platform designed for managing Clo projects and 3D assets. Closet functions similarly to Dropbox or Google Drive but is specialized for Clo users, enabling freelancers and hobbyists to organize, share, and collaborate on digital garment projects, fabrics, trims, avatars, and more. Closet serves as a centralized library for communication, presentation, and collection organization, accessible from anywhere. It supports real-time collaboration and feedback, making it ideal for managing 3D fashion design workflows remotely. --- ## Closet Structure and Organization within Roop Framework This section explains the organizational hierarchy and customization options within Closet, integrated into the Roop framework. Users can create companies, brands, and workrooms to structure their projects and collections effectively. - **Companies:** Top-level organizational unit. - **Brands:** Subdivisions within companies. - **Workrooms:** Spaces for organizing collections and client projects. Users can rename and reorganize their Closet folders beyond the default structure. For example, a demo structure might include a demo company, a demo brand, and a workroom like "Denim" to organize collections. --- ## Style Page Features and Project Version Management This section details the functionalities available on a style page, which is automatically created when a project is uploaded to Closet. The style page allows comprehensive management of project files and collaboration. - **Left Panel:** - Style information (date, creator, status, notifications) - Upload/download project or garment file versions - Generate tagpacks - Access render settings - File history to track project evolution and revert to previous versions - **Center Panel:** - 3D viewport with turntable preview - Annotation tools for commenting or drawing directly on the 3D model - Colorway switching for design variations - **Right Panel:** - List of all comments and annotations - Colorways and attachments - Shared access details Closet maintains strict access control: only invited users can view or edit content. The administrator can edit or delete any content and assign roles: - **Editors:** Can upload and download files they added. - **Viewers:** Can only view content, no editing rights. --- ## Cloud Rendering Capabilities in Closet Closet includes a cloud rendering service that allows users to render 3D garments without relying on local hardware. This is particularly useful for users with low-spec computers or when wanting to free up the local CLO license. - Rendering jobs run on Closet servers. - Completed renders are accessible on the style page. - Users can continue working locally while rendering occurs remotely. - Render outputs can be used directly to create or update styles. --- ## Visual Boards for Mood Boards and Design Showcases This section covers the Visual Board feature, which enables users to create interactive mood boards and design presentations using 3D assets from Closet. - Accessible from the user dashboard outside of workrooms and style pages. - Drag-and-drop 3D components from the content browser. - Customize backgrounds, add shapes, and insert text. - Final boards can include interactive links connected to underlying assets. - Eliminates the need for separate portfolio or visual workspace tools. --- ## Filtering and Searching Projects within Closet Closet provides powerful filtering and search options to efficiently navigate large libraries and collections: - Filter by workrooms, entire libraries, or specific categories such as product groups. - Search using custom tags assigned to styles. - Quickly get overviews, such as all styles marked for adoption into final collections. These features streamline workflow management and collection curation. --- ## Additional Resources For further details on Closet features and advanced functionalities, users are encouraged to consult in-depth tutorials and skill apps available on the Clo YouTube channel.
